?  Something doesn't look right here.  We're now completely ignoring the setpoint?

I have updated the code, commit message, and validation logs.

I’ve implemented xyz.openbmc_project.Debug.Stepwise.ThermalPower to ensure there is no impact on the existing xyz.openbmc_project.Debug.Pid.ThermalPower interface.

Please note that the Setpoint property is not applicable to Stepwise controllers, but the other properties align with the standard PID controller interface.

Please review. Thanks.
Done
why not just init to empty?

Initializing it from _inputs.front() ensures that updateThermalPowerDebugInterface always receives a valid input name, even when all sensors return NaN, so that the 'Input' property is updated instead of falling back to 'Output'.
Done
then just handle that case.  As written this code crashes if the list is empty.  You did the range check on line 101, but that's too late here.
Done
`class`?

Good question — the underscore is there because class is a C++ keyword.

It indicates what the loop is controlling, e.g. "Temperature", "Margin", "Power", or "PowerSum".
